questions.q:
$The $pH$ of a solution obtained by mixing $50mL$ of $1MHCl$ and $30mL$ of $1MNaOH$ is $x \times {10}^{- 4} .$~The value of $x$ is (Nearest integer)
\left[log2 . 5 = 0 . 3979\right]$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Milli equivalents of $HCl\left({N}_{a}{V}_{a}\right) = 50 \times 1 = 50$
Milli equivalents of $NaOH\left({N}_{b}{V}_{b}\right) = 30 \times 1 = 30$
Since ${N}_{a}{V}_{a} > {N}_{b}{V}_{b}$
\left[H^{+}\right] = \dfrac{{N}_{a}{V}_{a} - {N}_{b}{V}_{b}}{{V}_{a} + {V}_{b}} = \dfrac{50 - 30}{80} = \dfrac{20}{80} = 0 . 25 = 2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 1}$
$pH = - log\left[H^{+}\right] = - log\left(2 . 5 \times {10}^{- 1}\right) = 1 - 0 . 3979 = 0 . 6021$
$pH \times {10}^{4} = 0 . 6021 \times {10}^{4} = 6021

questions.q: At $310K$, the solubility of ${CaF}_{2}$ in water is $2 . 34 \times {10}^{- 3}g / 100mL$. The solubility product of ${CaF}_{2}$ is ----~$\times {10}^{- 8}\left(mol / L\right)3$(nearest integer). (Given molar mass : ${CaF}_{2} = 78g{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The solubility product constant is the equilibrium constant for the dissolution of a solid substance into an aqueous solution. It is denoted by the symbol ${K}_{sp}$.

Solubility of ${CaF}_{2} = Smole / / L$

$S = \dfrac{2 . 34 \times {10}^{- 3}}{0 . 1 \times 78} = \dfrac{2 . 34}{78} \times {10}^{- 2} = 3 \times {10}^{- 4}mol / L$

${K}_{sp}\left({CaF}_{2}\right) = 4S^{3} = 4\left(3 \times {10}^{- 4}\right)3$

$= 108 \times {10}^{- 12}$

$= 0 . 0108 \times {10}^{- 8}\left(mol / L\right)3$

questions.q:
A litre of buffer solution contains $0 . 1$~mole of each of ${NH}_{3}$~and ${NH}_{4}Cl$. On the addition of $0 . 02$~mole of $HCl$ by dissolving gaseous $HCl$, the $pH$ of the solution is found to be _____ \times {10}^{- 3}$~(Nearest integer)

Given:~${pK}_{b}\left({NH}_{3}\right) = 4 . 745$

$log2 = 0 . 301$

$log3 = 0 . 477$

$T = 298K ]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In resultant solution after addition of& $HCl$~to the basic buffer:

${n}_{NH3} = 0 . 1 - 0 . 02 = 0 . 08$

${n}_{{NH}_{4}Cl} = n{NH}_{4}^{+} = 0 . 1 + 0 . 02 = 0 . 12$

Using Henderson-Hasselbach equation:

$pOH = {pK}_{b} + log \left[{NH}_{4}^{+}\right]\left[{NH}_{3}\right]

$= 4 . 745 + $log\dfrac{0 . 12}{0 . 08}

$= 4 . 745 + $log\dfrac{3}{2}

$= 4 . 745 + 0 . 477 - 0 . 301$

$pOH = 4 . 921$
We know,

$pH = 14 - pH$

$= 9 . 079$

$

questions.q:
$0 . 01$ moles of a weak acid $HA \left({K}_{a} =$2 . 0 $\times {10}^{- 6}\right) is dissolved in $1 . 0L$ of $0 . 1MHCl$ solution. The degree of dissociation of $HA$ is~__________~\times {10}^{- 5} (Round off to the Nearest Integer). [Neglect volume change on adding $HA$~and assume degree of dissociation $< < 1$]

$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$\begin{cases}HA ⇌ H^{+} + & A^{-} & \\ \text{Initial conc.} & 0 . 1M & 0M & \\ \text{Equ. conc.} & ( 0 . 01 - x ) ( 0 . 1 + x ) & xM & \\ \approx 0 . 01M \approx 0 . 1M & \end{cases}$

Now,~${K}_{a} = \dfrac{\left[H^{+}\right]\left[A^{-}\right]}{[ HA ]} ⇒ 2 \times {10}^{- 6} = \dfrac{0 . 1 \times x}{0 . 01}$

$∴ x = 2 \times {10}^{- 7}$

Now,~$\alpha = \dfrac{x}{0 . 01} = \dfrac{2 \times {10}^{- 7}}{0 . 01} = 2 \times {10}^{- 5}$

If 1 mM solution of ethylamine produces $\mathrm{pH}=9$, then the ionization constant  \left(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}\right)$ of ethylamine is $10^{-x}$. The value of $x$ is ______ (nearest integer).
[The degree of ionization of ethylamine can be neglected with respect to unity.]$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution: Given, $\mathrmP^{\mathrm{H}}=9 \Rightarrow \mathrmP^{\mathrm{OH}}=5 \Rightarrow[\stackrel{\ominus}{\mathrm{OH}}]=10^{-5} \mathrm{M}$ Now, $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}=\frac{\left[\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{NH}_3^{+}\right][\stackrel{\ominus}{\mathrm{O}} \mathrm{H}]}{\left[\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{NH}_2\right]}\Rightarrow K_{\mathrm{b}}=\frac{10^{-5} \times 10^{-5}}{10^{-3}}=10^{-7}$

questions.q: The $pH$ at which $Mg ( OH{)}_{2} \left[{K}_{sp} =$1 $\times {10}^{- 11}\right] begins to precipitate from a solution containing $0 . 10M{Mg}^{2 +}$ ions is ______.$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Precipitation when ${Q}_{} = {K}_{sp}$

$Q =$Reaction quotient, it is the ratio of products to reactants at any time of reaction.

${K}_{sp} =$Solubility product.

$Mg\left(OH\right)2 ⇋ {Mg}^{2 +} + 2{OH}^{-}$

\left[{Mg}^{2 +}\right]\left[{OH}^{-}\right]2 = {10}^{- 11}$

$0 . 1 \times \left[{OH}^{-}\right]2 = {10}^{- 11} ⇒ \left[{OH}^{-}\right] = {10}^{- 5}$

$⇒ pOH = 5 ⇒ pH = 14 - 5 = 9$

$

If the concentration of acetic acid in the buffer is $1 . 0M,$~the concentration of sodium acetate in the buffer is ______M .$ (Round off to the Nearest Integer).~  \left[Given: pKa \left(\text{acetic acid}\right) =4 . 74\right]$

questions.q: An analyst wants to convert $1LHCl$~of $pH = 1$ to a solution of $HCl$~of $pH = 2$. The volume of water needed to do this dilution is _____ $mL$. (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The concentration of $H^{+}$~or say $HCl$~in both the given solution is ${10}^{– 1}$ and ${10}^{– 2}$ mole $L^{– 1}$ respectively.

For the given amount of $HCl$~the concentration depends over dilution hence

${M}_{1}{V}_{1} = {M}_{2}{V}_{2}\dfrac{M1}{M2} = \dfrac{V2}{V1}$

$\dfrac{10- 1}{10- 2} = \dfrac{V2}{1L}$

${V}_{2} = 10L = 10000mL$

$∆ V = 10000 - 1000mL = 9000mL$

questions.q:
The solubility product of ${BaSO}_{4}$~is $1 \times {10}^{- 10}$ at $298K$. The solubility of ${BaSO}_{4}$~in $0 . 1M{K}_{2}{SO}_{4} ( aq )$ solution is~ ~ ------$\times {10}^{- 9}gL^{- 1}$(nearest integer).
Given: Molar mass of ${BaSO}_{4}$~is $233g{mol}^{- 1}$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
For the insoluble salt barium sulphate, sulphate ion added is the common ion. Due to the common& ion effect the solubility of barium sulphate decreases. Let us assume solubility of barium sulphate is& $S$.

${BaSO}_{4} \left(s\right) ⇌ \mathop{Ba2 +}_{S} \left($aq\right) + \mathop{SO42 -}_{S + 0 . $1}\left($aq\right)$
$\mathop{{K}_{2}{SO}_{4}}_{0 . 1 - 0 . 1} ⟶ \mathop{K^{+}}_{0 . 1} \left(aq\right) + \mathop{SO42 -}_{0 . 1}\left(aq\right)$
${K}_{SP} = \left[{Ba}^{2 +}\right] \left[{SO}_{4}^{2 -}\right]
$1 $\times {10}^{- 10} =$S ( S + 0 . 1 )$
$≃ 0 . 1S$
$S = {10}^{- 9}M = 233 $\times {10}^{- 9}{gL}^{- 1}

questions.q:
Millimoles of calcium hydroxyide required to produce $100mL$ of the aqueous solution of $pH12$~is $x \times {10}^{- 1}$. The value of $x$ is _____ (Nearest integer).
Assume complete dissociation.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
We know,
$pH = - log [ H^{+} ]$~,~$pH = - log [ {OH}^{-} ] , pH + pOH = 14$
$∵ pH = 12$

$∴ \left[H^{+}\right] = {10}^{- 12}M$

$∴ \left[{OH}^{-}\right] = {10}^{- 2}M$
We also know,
$Ca ( OH{)}_{2} ⇌ 2{OH}^{-} + {Ca}^{2 +}$

$∴ \left[Ca ( OH{)}_{2}\right] = 5 \times {10}^{- 3}M$

$5 \times {10}^{- 3} = \dfrac{\text{milli moles of}Ca\left(OH\right)2}{100mL}$

milli moles of $Ca\left(OH\right)2 = 5 \times {10}^{- 1}$

Ans. $= 5$

questions.q:
The titration curve of weak acid vs. strong base with phenolphthalein as indicator& is shown below. The& ${K}_{phenolphthalein } = 4 \times {10}^{- 10}$

Given: $log2 = 0 . 3$

The number of following statement/s which is/are correct about phenolphthalein is _______

A. It can be used as an indicator for the titration of weak acid with weak base.

B. It begins to change colour at $pH = 8 . 4$

C. It is a weak organic base

D. It is colourless in acidic medium
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Phenolphthalein is an organic acid and can be represented as $HPh$.

$\mathop{HPh}_{ (colourless) } ⇌ H^{+} + \mathop{Ph -}_{ (Pink) }$

Using Henderson equation for phenolphthalein

$pH = {pK}_{In} + log \left[ \left[{Ph}^{-}\right][$HPh ]\right]$

At equivalence point \left[{Ph}^{-}\right] = [$HPh ]$

$∴ {pH}_{2} = {pK}_{In} = - log [ 4 ] + 10 = - 0 . 6 + 10 = 9 . 4$

Hence at $( 9 . 4 \pm1 ) PH$~, phenolphthalein starts changing colour. Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic medium and pink in basic medium. Phenolphthalein indicator distinguish the pH change between~$8$~to~$10$. Therefore, it is used for strong acid and strong base titration or weak acid and strong base titration. Hence, A and C are incorrect statements.

!$

questions.q:
At $298K$, the solubility of silver chloride in water is $1 . 434 \times {10}^{- 3}gL^{- 1}$. The value of $- {logK}_{sp}$ for silver chloride is
(Given mass of Ag is $107 . 9g{mol}^{- 1}$, and mass of $Cl$ is $35 . 5g{mol}^{- 1}$ )
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Formula unit mass of Silver chloride =& $108 + 35 . 5{gmol}^{- 1} = 143 . 5{gmol}^{- 1}$
Solubility$( s ) = \dfrac{1 . 434}{143 . 4} \times {10}^{- 3} = {10}^{- 5}M$

$∴ {K}_{sp} ( AgCl ) = [ Ag ] [ Cl ] = ( s{)}^{2}$

$⇒ {K}_{sp} ( AgCl ) = {10}^{- 10}$

$⇒ - log\left({K}_{sp}\right) = 10$

questions.q: The $pH$ of ammonium phosphate solution, if ${pk}_{a}$ of phosphoric acid and ${pk}_{b}$ of ammonium hydroxide are $5 . 23$ and $4 . 75$ respectively, is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Since \left({NH}_{4}\right)3{PO}_{4}$ is salt of weak acid \left({H}_{3}{PO}_{4}\right)$~and weak base \left({NH}_{4}OH\right)$

$pH = 7 + \dfrac{1}{2} \left(pka - pkb\right)$

$= 7 + $\dfrac{1}{2} \left(5 . 23 - 4 . 75\right)$

$= 7 . 24 \approx 7$

questions.q: $25 . 0mL$ of $0 . 050MBa\left({NO}_{3}\right)2$~is mixed with $25 . 0mL$ of~$0 . 020MNaF . {K}_{sp}$~of ${BaF}_{2}$~is $0 . 5 \times 10 – 6$~at $298K .$ The ratio of \left[{Ba}^{2 +}\right]\left[F^{-}\right]2$~and ${K}_{sp}$~is~______ .$
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Given:

Volume of $Ba ( {NO}_{3}{)}_{2}$ solution = $25 . 0$mL~ Concentration of $Ba ( {NO}_{3}{)}_{2}$ solution = $0 . 050$M Volume of $NaF$ solution = $25 . 0$mL~ Concentration of $NaF$ solution = $0 . 020$M

\left[{Ba}^{+ 2}\right] = \left(\dfrac{25 \times 0 . 05}{50}\right) = 0 . 025M$

\left[F^{-}\right] = \left(\dfrac{25 \times 0 . 02}{50}\right) =$0 . 01M$

\left[{Ba}^{+ 2}\right]~\left[$F^{-}\right] = 25 $\times {10}^{- 7}

${K}_{sp} = 0 . 5 $\times {10}^{- 6} =$5 $\times {10}^{- 7}

Ratio=\dfrac{\left[{Ba}^{+ 2}\right]\left[F^{-}\right]}{Ksp} = \dfrac{25 \times {10}^{- 7}}{5 \times {10}^{- 7}} =$5$

$

questions.q:
$600mL$ of $0 . 01MHCl$ is mixed with $400mL$ of $0 . 01M{H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$. The $pH$ of the mixture is _____\times {10}^{- 2}$. (Nearest integer)

[Given $log2 = 0 . 30, log3 = 0 . 48, log5 = 0 . 69, log7 = 0 . 84, log11 = 1 . 04]
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The number of millimoles = $Molarity \times Volume$ in~$mL$

$HCl$~produce one and~${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$~produce two~$H^{+}$~ions respectively.

Total milimoles of $H^{+} = \left(600 \times 0 . 01\right) + \left(400 \times 0 . 01 \times 2\right) = 14$
Thus, moles of hydrogen ion:
$⇒ \left[H^{+}\right] = \dfrac{14}{1000} = 14 \times {10}^{- 3}$
$⇒ pH = - log [ H^{+} ] = - log [ 14 \times {10}^{- 3} ]$

$⇒ pH = 3 - log14$

$= 1 . 86$

$= 186 \times {10}^{- 2}$
